scope_entries.finding: resolve_state_dir (state.py:489), the 0700 helper (state.py:550), the atomic temp+rename writer (state.py:698) and the stale-temp sweep (state.py:875) all exist and are reusable; no inbox, spool or ingest code exists anywhere in embodiment/ (grep)

upsert is load, mutate, atomic replace with no cross-process lock and one shared .tmp name; continuity._STORE_LOCK (continuity.py:352) is an in-process RLock held for every eidetic call, so a second writing process would lose updates

the only periodic tick is pump() every poll_interval_s=0.5 (app.py:1404-1418); close(deadline) hands out cumulative shares (summary first, memory 0.98, app.py:1461-1479), so a drain needs its own bounded step and a close share
an existing test class already guards the store lock against stalling a turn; the drain must extend it rather than bypass it

recall is hard-bound to the one scope fixed at construction, and eidetic serves a private record only to the same scope name and visibility, so a gwen-recordings record is invisible to Gwen today without a memory.py change
the header label charset is [A-Za-z0-9._-]; the proposed id `pocket:<rec>:<kind>:<n>` contains ':' and would render as placeholder characters, and _safe_record_id (app.py:3686) would refuse it

recall only hides records whose stored lifecycle is shadowed/archived; writing A with supersedes=B does not hide B until a sweep runs, and nothing in embodiment calls sweep; the default sweep also archives records older than 365 days or with signal below 0.25
RoomMemory.remember emits only id, text, type, created, metadata, added_by — no supersedes, links, lifecycle or scope — although continuity._build_record (continuity.py:690-734) would accept them
for a new id, upsert drops every existing record in the scope file with the same text hash before appending — the older id is silently deleted; hash is SHA-256 of text, not metadata.content_hash

eidetic has no archive/forget verb; facet filters on metadata exist but recall is ranked and query-bound, so backend.all() is the only true enumeration; archive is embodiment's continuity.archive, by id, one scope

culture-rules forgets on recording.deleted by --source-id, forgets source then re-distils target on merged, and when a re-distil yields fewer facts it forgets the surplus ids — by id, which #94 does not specify

render_recalled renders only id, added_by, created and quoted text; metadata and type are never rendered, and the fuzzer never generates metadata, so title/date/timestamp provenance is a new rendered surface the fence test does not cover

tools dispatch only from model tool_calls; the daemon binds exactly remember and forget; recall enters at one point, the end of the system prompt — the residual risk is prompt-level persuasion, which #89 (a future do tool) makes worse
pocketsync is the source of truth; Gwen's records are a distilled projection, content changes arrive only through the queue, Gwen never edits or enriches them herself
ingest only enqueues; records are stored for recall, never pushed into a live prompt; an optional operator-toggled metadata-only digest is offered

machine.command runs a local Popen with _MINIMAL_ENV {PATH, LANG}, stdin=DEVNULL, a fresh temp cwd, fixed argv templates with {param} substitution; non-zero exit = failed (retryable), stdout is not parsed, 60 s default timeout
--state-dir is the established override flag; lifecycle.status() reports running/stopped and the state_dir actually in use, including a fallback dir
supports_idempotency_key = False; #73 comment 3 says runner steps should be declared idempotent so unsafe_retry does not block retries
the only outbound event types are recording.enriched and recording.reclassified; recording.deleted/merged are inbound Pocket webhooks handled by tombstoning in the sinks with no event emitted

one nested-noun precedent exists (cli overview, parser_class=type(p)); the introspection test walks the parser recursively and fails on any uncatalogued path; no verb has --apply today (tunnel is dry-run only)

routes are only events, status, voice start/stop and mic mute; Controls has four callables; the daemon has run_turn (app.py:2143) and submit_transcript (app.py:2074) but no HTTP route reaches them; the dashboard has no text input

AssertionVerifier = Callable[[str], AssertionResult]; the default refuses every token; the refusal status is hard-coded 401 so a 503 needs a status field or code; main() builds Guard with no assertion_verifier — the single wiring point

stdlib-only RS256 via pow, kid-keyed JWKS cache with rate-limited refetch, negative cache and single-flight; reasons include unavailable (server maps to 503); itself cited from culture-rules culture_rules/auth/access.py, which mirrors culture-nodes internal/auth/verifier.go
a stdlib-only verifier adds no third-party import and needs no pin change; it must use urllib, not the httpx that coherence-cli brings in
Host, Origin, then the install secret, then the assertion when Host is public — a verified Access identity does not relax the secret check
